Context preparation is not a model planning stage. Before session open, hash/index explicitly selected package and release files and known supplier/part records. After opening, apply case facts, live messages, current quote standards and document records. A new live event yields a new context version. Semantic retrieval and assessor choice can later vary, while the underlying evidence records remain available.

Initial scope: delivery and commitment exchanges, keep current package, bounded clarification question, and request deterministic closing evaluation. Never promise volume outside schema. Requests for cost breakdown/schedule and deterministic workbook extraction are follow-on capabilities, not mandatory model tools in the first loop. Adverse facts stay in the internal assessment even when outward claim policy chooses not to disclose them.

The model interpreter returns observations and separately labelled hypotheses. Code checks citation existence, supplier scope, exact message spans, enum values and schema; semantic correctness needs independent labels/tests. The initial capacity policy proposes intents only for supported dimensions, retains a baseline intent, and excludes known refused exchanges without new evidence. Candidate generation derives numeric prices/terms entirely in code and reports why an intent is infeasible. Candidate selection receives economic values and uncertainty as private decision inputs; an external model receives only the permitted projection in C.

Closing is a separate deterministic path. `agreed`, final offers, rounds exhaustion, explicit close requests, and deadline admission all use the same all-thread eligibility and economic comparison. Models can request that comparison; they cannot bind an accept or walk-away. The coordinator has sole closing ownership.

## 5. State, persistence and restart

Use a versioned event log with a materialized `NegotiationState`. Events are immutable; snapshots are derived and replaceable. Each event has a run/session identity, unique event ID, monotone local sequence, parent/correlation IDs, source timestamp when available, receipt timestamp, schema version and typed payload. Deduplicate official messages by session/thread/message ID; if missing, use a documented stable fingerprint and flag ambiguity. Arrival order does not prove commercial causality.

Keep three separate projections:

| Projection | Authority and content |
|---|---|
| Server | Session/thread status, standing sheets, accepted messages, counted rounds/deadline evidence, terminal proof; only gateway observations modify it |
| Strategic | Assessments, attempted intents, candidate/decision linkage, refusals, outstanding questions, evidence outcomes, final-offer observation evidence; no server truth override |
| Operational | Outbox ownership, exact payload/ID, validation basis, pending/uncertain requests, local run health; an operational failure is not a commercial walk-away |

SQLite commits events, a new head version, claim reservations, and an operation together. Use compare-and-swap against the input head version and source/config/context fingerprints. Never hold a transaction/lock over model inference, document parsing, limiter waits or HTTP. A stale proposal is discarded or recomputed. A late answer from a cancelled model call cannot mutate state.

Persist raw observations plus bounded validated model artifacts; do not persist private chain-of-thought. Alternative interpreters can derive their own assessment revisions from the same source history. Strategy-specific memory is schema-versioned and namespaced; the first slice needs only generic attempted/refused-exchange records. It is not an untyped mutable blob.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Prepared
    Prepared --> Ready: sources/config admitted; session opened or recovered
    Ready --> Deciding: immutable snapshot
    Deciding --> Ready: stale/invalid proposal; no dispatch
    Deciding --> OperationPrepared: atomic validated intent commit
    OperationPrepared --> Awaiting: dispatch exact payload
    OperationPrepared --> Ready: proven never dispatched; release reservation
    Awaiting --> Ready: acknowledged reply; observations/feedback committed
    Awaiting --> RecoveryRequired: outcome unknown / operational budget exhausted
    RecoveryRequired --> Ready: proven rejection or reconciled reply
    RecoveryRequired --> Awaiting: admitted same-ID replay
    Ready --> Closing: deterministic fresh close decision
    Closing --> Awaiting: owned close operation prepared and submitted
    Awaiting --> Ended: authoritative terminal proof
    RecoveryRequired --> Ended: server terminal proof reconciled
    Ended --> [*]
```

On restart: verify run/config ownership; load snapshot and replay later events; preserve pending operation and reservations; fetch permitted server state; reconcile before any new POST. Refusal history and sent/acknowledged attempts survive. Monotonic process times are never restored. Unknown rounds or uncertain remote outcome require recovery, not a fresh session or reset memory.

Legacy JSONL is read/imported without modification. Preserve unknown/abandoned legacy operations as historical ambiguous records unless there is proof of their disposition. Importing an old `result` does not create terminal proof. Existing Lab records keep original and recovered outcomes separately. New V2 storage does not retroactively “repair” old scores.

## 6. Validation, disclosure and economic authority

Incoming partial supplier sheets are preserved exactly as observed. Resolve closing defaults separately using official precedence: buyer defaults -> quote standards -> fixed case terms -> explicit sheet. Validate explicit fields before allowing them to override fixed/schema authority. Keep resolved commercial terms and transmitted negotiable terms as distinct typed values.

Supplier valuation uses a different reference: current quote standards override dossier/master defaults field by field. It must not accidentally use buyer closing defaults as the supplier reference. Both views are versioned and derived from the same evidence sources.

At every outgoing boundary, require: legal action kind; exact negotiable field set for offer sheets; allowed options or verified standards exception; positive finite two-decimal price; correct type/basis; must-haves; finite official complete cost; compatible claims/disclosure; recipient/session/standing-offer ownership; current state; admitted timing/rounds; no unresolved conflicting operation; and protocol payload limits. Final rendering happens before validation. Replayed operations cannot bypass state/economic validity checks, and their ID/payload cannot be mutated to repair a rejection.

Offer price numbers may be private-model-visible candidate values, but official economic calculations, reservation values, targets, lack of alternatives, urgency, and internal estimates are never passed wholesale to a writer or included in outgoing prose. Models see a purpose-specific projection. Document text may itself contain private values; field allowlisting alone is insufficient. Attachments and snippets require a reviewed disclosure classification. The first slice uses selected contextual snippets with provenance and no arbitrary original-file export.

Evidence classes distinguish canonical records, supplier statements, and internal estimates/hypotheses. A document can authoritatively establish that a supplier wrote a statement without making the statement true. Numeric supplier attachments are source-attributed observations unless independently verified. Missing/future/stale/incompatible facts remain explicit gaps. Relevance ranking must not remove all adverse evidence from internal decision context.

Economic evaluations keep nominal official cost, full components, estimate version and sensitivity scenarios. Scenarios are not confidence intervals unless supported by a calibrated model. Missing executable alternative is a tagged value, not serialized infinity and not no-deal score. Operational fallback cost is separately evaluated. Initial no-alternative final policy closes on an eligible acceptable standing deal or continues only through an explicit bounded policy; it performs no undefined expected-loss arithmetic.

## 7. Budgets and reliability

One `DecisionBudget` applies across preparation of live inputs, interpretation, candidate work, selection, rendering, validation and limiter queue. Start from conservative clock evidence, charge elapsed time since observation, and reserve time for fallback and transport submission. Proposed initial local targets: buyer computation at most 35 s when the authoritative remaining window permits; interpreter at most 8 s; optional selector at most 4 s; at most two model requests per turn, with no automatic model retries. These are engineering targets to validate, not Arena guarantees.

HTTP phase timeout is separate from total operational deadline. Supplier generation may pause its buyer clock but does not create a fresh wave cap. If clock evidence is insufficient, disable expensive advice and use a conservative admitted action or recovery-required outcome. Do not let a cached reply start a new 60-second window. Store clock provenance and receive/request timestamps.

Transport timeout, cancellation and many retryable errors do not prove a POST failed. Bound reconciliation work, persist `uncertain`, return a resumable operational result, and retain ownership. A definite 422 can fail an operation; 409/5xx/quota errors require classification and server evidence, not a universal “failed” label. On final-state confirmation, distinguish whether a pending operation is proven applied, invalidated, or unresolved at terminal observation.

For initial use, one execution owner holds a team-key lease for the supported runtime and no other launcher uses that key concurrently. Normal CLI, adapted V1 and Lab must acquire the same admission lease on the chosen host. A multi-host deployment needs a shared authority; a local lock cannot protect independent laptops. This is an operational restriction, not a claim that a global broker is implemented.

Async RFQ admission later requires supervised task completion/errors, all-thread snapshots, no awaited state lock, bounded unresolved/watchdog exit, shared limiter/capacity, queued-case wave checks, and restart/transport tests. Do not enable async by merely relaxing the current adviser feature check.

## 8. Effective configuration and deployment

Resolve once before opening: schema/agent version, strategy proposal/selector bundle, interpreter implementation, template/claim versions, data/prep/case hashes, economics/estimate and closing policy, runtime mode, budgets/fallback, model protocol/identity/effort/sampling/timeout, allowed capabilities, endpoint identity, and recovery rules. Credentials are injected references and never serialized/hash inputs; operationally meaningful provider identity is recorded without keys.

Use explicit config file/arguments over documented environment mappings over checked-in defaults, reject unknown/incompatible options, and record origin and effective value. Legacy guidance is frozen into V1 config at resolution, not read differently by each factory. V2 ignores ambient legacy feature flags unless a named migration maps them. Model nondeterminism means equivalent config does not imply identical model decisions; deterministic parts must remain equivalent.

CLI and Lab use one factory. Add a versioned checkpoint envelope preserving the legacy schema and supporting agent implementation + resolved configuration + prep/source fingerprints. Reject V2 in an old worker before session open. Do not reinterpret old checkpoint hashes. V1 and V2 record distinct agent identities and trace versions; old viewers continue to open historical records.

Buyer orchestration continues to run where the command executes. The existing Lab server stores and displays records; it does not become a negotiation/model service by this plan. No new cloud deployment is needed for offline or single-owner local capacity testing. Later deployment selects a reviewed host and rehearses data, inference protocol, deadlines, lease, recovery and exact served revision separately from dashboard health.

## 9. Trace and explainability

Every turn links raw evidence/context version -> assessment revision -> intent IDs -> candidate IDs and rejection reasons -> nominal/scenario cost evaluations -> selected candidate -> close decision if requested -> final rendered payload -> validation -> operation ID and payload hash -> acknowledged/uncertain outcome -> response -> feedback/state revision.

Diagnostic traces preserve candidate versus selected versus validated versus submitted versus acknowledged distinctions. Only the operation payload is the authoritative sent record. A concise rationale with citations explains a proposal; it is not proof of correctness. Rejections and fallback paths receive the same linkage. Session and attempt IDs prevent one hosted dump from being reused across unrelated repeats.

Export JSONL and a Lab projection from the durable store. Keep private assessment/economic details in appropriately controlled inspection artifacts; public/shared exports apply a separate redaction policy. A failed export must not alter execution state. M6 adds an inspectable turn view to existing Lab, without rebuilding it.

## 9. Implementation refinements after architecture approval

The architecture is approved in principle. The initial scope and authority remain the same; C §8 now resolves the implementation choices. [Task specs](task-specs.md) and the executable suite are its implementation handoff. Add `adapters/official.py`, `adapters/claims.py`, and `adapters/recorded.py` to the module tree. Official/legacy imports live in adapters and are injected through core ports. This corrects the ambiguous idea that economics could directly import arena_kit while remaining independent of concrete infrastructure.

The module graph enforced by tests is: each feature package imports core and its own package; adapters import core/adapters plus existing libraries; config imports core/config; only factory imports selected concrete features. Root v2/__init__.py stays empty. No dynamic strategy import, eval/exec, network/process API outside adapters, or production import from tests. Inject collaborators to cross package boundaries. These checks are static import guards, supplemented by narrow capability injection; they do not pretend to prove absence of every possible side effect.

M1 must already connect recorded case → evidence context → typed mock assessment → proposed intent → generated candidate → official-cost/mock-certified evaluation → selection → rendering → validation → scripted execution → persisted feedback/result. Include immutable effective config, input versions, artifact hashes and DecisionRecord storage. Fake provider/server responses stay marked as fixtures. The first offline package/cost is a demo golden; no production supplier intelligence or recovery claim follows from it. M2–M5 replace mock ports incrementally under the same contracts. Basic integration and replay are not deferred to M5/M6.

Supplier assessment has four collections: observations, reported constraints, preference hypotheses and uncertainties. An observation records speech; a reported constraint is still an unverified supplier report; hypotheses may have opposing support; approval/conditional/contradictory gaps stay explicit. Assessment revisions are appended with parent references and their decision records preserve the version used. No interpreter mutates legal options, numeric costs or state.

DecisionRecord is a versioned immutable graph of all ten stages, including exact selected/evaluated identity, final validation/payload hash, owned operation, acknowledged/unknown execution and feedback. The SQLite record/artifact store starts in M1; operation/state/claim atomic commits extend it in M5. Generic structured assertions and typed term fields allow later strategy bundles/routers to consume these records without changing evidence, economics or execution. Future behavior models receive read-only historical assessment/feedback views; no learning machinery is part of this delivery.

Runtime defaults are one case owner and one outstanding operation. Rejected closes while authoritative status is open remain recovery_required. Unknown requests retain exact identity/bytes/reservations. Retry exhaustion does not abandon ownership. All closing triggers use the fresh shared close evaluator and final validator. Absolute deadlines and event-derived round evidence are explicit inputs. Serial first; async, shared cloud broker and multi-agent frameworks remain outside this implementation cutline.


## T1.1d field-contract finalization — 10 October 2026

C §8.9 finalizes the remaining fields within this architecture. It contains 146 concrete DTOs
and 14 closed union exports, grouped into 16 serial handoffs of at most 15 exports. The four
metadata DTOs and T1.1a–c foundation stay implemented; the remaining production schemas are
not implemented by this documentation/test task. This replaces the coarse four-category
handoff with smaller dependency-ordered assignments, not a new component architecture.

Typed SupplierStandards tuples and ScenarioPolicy/EstimateScenario remove mutable mapping
and estimate-policy ambiguities. A closed registered NamedEstimate enum distinguishes
hypothetical estimate values/units from source facts and executable economics. Typed feedback,
provider purpose projections and hydrated events preserve the existing port boundaries.
Models validate immutable shapes/local invariants; services still own source truth, full-cost
certification, registry-verified configuration, bytes/proofs, dispatch and official termination.

Every export has a concrete JSON example and positive/negative tests in the existing V2 suite.
The test-only `dto-contracts.json` is handoff data, never a runtime schema registry or production
model generator. Explicit --v2-dto-require batch gates prevent missing models being counted as
implementation. Copy-ready prompts and dependencies are in task-specs.md; later services,
storage, intelligence and runtime readiness still have their separate gates.

            or self.clock.utcnow() >= requested_at + timedelta(seconds=seconds)
        ):
            raise ContractViolation("deadline_exhausted: online dispatch lacks a current server window")
        expected_rounds = sum(e.get("from") == "buyer" for e in self.authoritative_threads[supplier_id])
        if rounds != expected_rounds:
            raise ContractViolation("stale_state: server-counted rounds changed or include unprocessed timeouts")
        if message.get("action", {}).get("type") == "accept" and (
            message["action"]["term_sheet_id"] != live.get("offer_id")
        ):
            raise ContractViolation("stale_state: live standing offer changed before closing")
        if message.get("action"):
            if self.pending_message != {"supplier_id": supplier_id, "message": message}:
                raise ContractViolation("invalid_schema: closing payload changed")
            self.closing.validate(self.pending_message, case=self.dataset["case"],
                                  threads=self.closing_threads(supplier_id, current_thread["messages"]))
            return
        return super().validate_lab_dispatch(supplier_id, message, current_thread)

    def thread_rounds(self, supplier):
        raw, _, _ = self.observed_server
        if type(raw.get("rounds")) is not int:
            raise ContractViolation("rounds_unknown: missing authoritative rounds/clock")
        if len(self.dataset["case"]["suppliers"]) == 1:
            return raw["rounds"]
        # Arena session rounds sum per-thread moves. Timeouts cannot be assigned from
        # that sum, so require the exact acknowledged total before admitting a move.
        counts = {sid: sum(e.get("from") == "buyer" for e in events)
                  for sid, events in self.authoritative_threads.items()}
        if set(counts) != set(self.dataset["case"]["suppliers"]) or sum(counts.values()) != raw["rounds"]:
            raise ContractViolation("stale_state: RFQ rounds require complete acknowledged histories without timeouts")
        return counts[supplier]

    def closing_threads(self, supplier, events):
        return {**self.authoritative_threads, supplier: events}

    def select_lab_supplier(self, case, threads):
        raw, _, _ = self.observed_server
        eligible = [sid for sid in case["suppliers"]
                    if raw["threads"][sid].get("status") not in {"walked_away", "no_bid", "ended"}]
        if not eligible:
            raise ContractViolation("invalid_terminal_proof: no live supplier; retrieve terminal result")
        return min(eligible, key=lambda sid: (self.thread_rounds(sid), raw["threads"][sid]["seconds_left"], sid))

    def decision_dataset(self, supplier):
        # The arithmetic oracle remains one-supplier/one-part. Each target receives a
        # faithful economic slice; the case coordinator compares every live bidder.
        case = {**self.dataset["case"], "suppliers": [supplier]}
        candidates = self.dataset.get("candidate_terms_by_supplier", {}).get(supplier, self.dataset["candidate_terms"])
        return {**self.dataset, "case": case, "candidate_terms": candidates}

    def should_close(self, case, supplier, events, count):
        raw, requested_at, _ = self.observed_server
        elapsed = (self.clock.utcnow() - requested_at).total_seconds()
        live = [sid for sid in case["suppliers"]
                if raw["threads"][sid].get("status") in {"open", "final_offer", "agreed"}]
        if any(raw["threads"][sid]["seconds_left"] - elapsed <= 15 for sid in live):
            return True
        interviewed = all(self.thread_rounds(sid) > 0 for sid in live)
        return (count >= case["round_limit"] - 1 or
                interviewed and any(raw["threads"][sid].get("status") == "agreed" for sid in live))

    def prior_market_evidence(self, supplier):
        # Public observed rival packages inform internal comparison only. Renderer
        # sends validated own packages; it does not disclose these notes to suppliers.
        import json

        return ("Buyer category goal: " + self.dataset["case"]["buyer"]["category_goal"] +
                "; supplier full costs are unestimated; do not infer a hidden floor or sustainable margin.",) + tuple(
                     "Observed rival standing package: " + json.dumps({"supplier_id": sid,
                     "term_sheets": events[-1].get("term_sheets", [])}, sort_keys=True)
                     for sid, events in self.authoritative_threads.items() if sid != supplier and events)

    def observe_lab_outcome(self, result, threads):
        import json

        from arena_kit.docs import read_document

        from negotiator.lab.publish import _atomic_file

        from .arena_observations import conversation_from_arena

        conversations = {}
        for sid, thread in threads.items():
            for event in thread["messages"]:
                for att in event.get("attachments", []):
                    att["text"] = read_document(att["name"], self.attachment_bytes[att["attachment_id"]])
            conversations[sid] = conversation_from_arena(self.dataset["case"], thread["messages"],
                session_id=self.session_id, supplier_id=sid, now=self.clock.utcnow(),
                attachment_bytes=self.attachment_bytes).model_dump(mode="json")
        self.terminal_evidence = {"state": self.terminal_state, "result": result, "conversations": conversations}
        _atomic_file(self.trace_root / self.run_id / self.session_id / "terminal-observation.json",
                     json.dumps(self.terminal_evidence, indent=2))

    def experiment_evidence(self):
        import json

        evidence = super().experiment_evidence()
        evidence["observations_json"] = [o.model_dump_json() for o in self.observations]
        evidence["terminal_json"] = json.dumps(getattr(self, "terminal_evidence", None), sort_keys=True)
        evidence["inference_ledger_json"] = json.dumps(getattr(self.transport, "calls", []), sort_keys=True)
        return evidence

async def run_recorded_decision(
    inputs: OfflineRecordedInputs,
    *,
    assembler: OfflineContextAssembler,
    coordinator: OfflineDecisionCoordinator,
) -> OfflineDecisionTrace:
    inputs = load_recorded_json(inputs.model_dump_json())
    snapshot = assembler.assemble(inputs)
    return await coordinator.run_once(
        snapshot, previous_assessment=inputs.previous_assessment, recorded_input_bytes=canonical_json(inputs)
    )


def bounded_services(inputs, clock, transport=None, config=None, *, prompt_revision="v1", arm="grounded",
                     prior_evaluations=()):
    """Same bounded ports for recorded inputs and the local Lab bridge."""
    evaluator = OfficialEconomicEvaluator(oracle=OfficialArithmetic())
    from .evidence.resolver import LayeredEvidenceResolver

    assembler = OfflineContextAssembler(
        context_builder=LayeredContextBuilder(resolver=LayeredEvidenceResolver(admit_live_quotes=True)),
        projections=EvidenceProjections(),
        estimate_builder=SourceCostEstimateBuilder(),
    )
    supplier = inputs.target_supplier_id
    interpreter = InputEchoTestInterpreter(supplier_id=supplier)
    selector = MinimumCostTestSelector()
    proposal = SuppliedIntentTestPolicy(supplier_id=supplier, include_question=True)
    generator = SuppliedCandidateGenerator(packages=inputs.packages)
    if transport is not None:
        gateway = AsyncModelGateway(transport=transport)
        hashes = tuple(msg.content_hash for msg in inputs.server.threads[0].conversation.messages)
        ic = InterpreterConfig(
            provider_id=config.provider_id,
            protocol_id=config.protocol_id,
            model_id=config.model_id,
            prompt_version="grounded-supplier-" + prompt_revision,
            task_schema_version="assessment-citation-ids-v1" if prompt_revision == "v3" else "assessment-draft-v1",
            max_tokens=98304 if arm == "adaptive" else 16384,
            time_limit_s=Decimal("8"),
            approved_message_hashes=hashes,
            max_input_chars=64000 if prompt_revision == "v3" else 16000,
        )
        sc = SelectorConfig(
            **{
                **ic.model_dump(),
                "prompt_version": "grounded-selection-" + ("v2" if prompt_revision == "v3" else prompt_revision),
                "task_schema_version": "selector-response-v1",
                "time_limit_s": Decimal("4"),
                "full_observations": prompt_revision == "v3",
                "max_input_chars": 64000 if prompt_revision == "v3" else 16000,
            }
        )
        if arm in {"grounded", "adaptive"}:
            interpreter = GroundedInterpreter(model=gateway, clock=clock, config=ic)
        selector = BoundedModelSelector(model=gateway, clock=clock, config=sc)
        if arm == "adaptive":
            from .strategy.proposal import BoundedProposalPolicy, ProposalSelector, ProposedCandidateGenerator
            proposal = BoundedProposalPolicy(model=gateway, clock=clock, config=ic, evaluator=evaluator,
                                             projector=project, prior_evaluations=prior_evaluations)
            generator = ProposedCandidateGenerator(fallback=generator)
            selector = ProposalSelector()
    coordinator = OfflineDecisionCoordinator(
        interpreter=interpreter,
        proposal=proposal,
        generator=generator,
        evaluator=evaluator,
        selector=selector,
        renderer_factory=lambda batch: TemplateActionRenderer(batch=batch),
        validator=FinalActionValidator(evaluator=evaluator, clock=clock),
        payload_encoder=payload_bytes,
        clock=clock,
        model_token_limit=(196608 if arm == "adaptive" else 32768) if transport is not None else None,
    )
    return assembler, coordinator



def local_lab_agent(*, dataset_path, trace_root, arm="grounded", clock=None, transport=None,
                    closing_authority=False, model_config=None):
    """Explicit opt-in local Lab composition; remote execution remains unavailable."""
    from .adapters.lab import LocalV2LabAgent
    from .orchestration.metrics import decision_metrics

    return LocalV2LabAgent(dataset_path=dataset_path, trace_root=trace_root, arm=arm,
                           clock=clock, transport=transport, runtime_builder=bounded_services,
                           run_decision=run_recorded_decision, metrics=decision_metrics,
                           closing_authority=closing_authority, model_config=model_config)


def online_lab_agent(*, dataset_path, trace_root, transport, model_config, execution_allowance, clock=None):
    """Explicitly approved P10 composition for the existing tracked Lab runner only."""
    from .adapters.online import VerifiedOnlineV2LabAgent
    from .orchestration.metrics import decision_metrics

    return VerifiedOnlineV2LabAgent(dataset_path=dataset_path, trace_root=trace_root, arm="adaptive",

L53: L54: [Button: Create GitHub issue for staff review] L55: L56: * * * L57: ##### Abstract L58: Much of human dialogue occurs in semi-cooperative settings, where agents with different goals attempt to agree on common decisions. Negotiations require complex communication and reasoning skills, but success is easy to measure, making this an interesting task for AI. We gather a large dataset of human-human negotiations on a multi-issue bargaining task, where agents who cannot observe each other’s reward functions must reach an agreement (or a deal) via natural language dialogue. L59: For the first time, we show it is possible to train end-to-end models for negotiation, which must learn both linguistic and reasoning skills with no annotated dialogue states. We also introduce dialogue rollouts, in which the model plans ahead by simulating possible complete continuations of the conversation, and find that this technique dramatically improves performance. Our code and dataset are publicly available. def project(context, conversation, supplier_id, config):
    """Fail closed on unsupported history; never rewrite a source under its hash."""
    if conversation.session_id != context.snapshot.session_id:
        raise ContractViolation("scope_mismatch: foreign conversation")
    total = 0
    full = config.prompt_version.endswith("-v3")
    for msg in conversation.messages:
        total += len(msg.body)
        if ((msg.speaker not in {"supplier", "buyer", "arena"} if full else msg.speaker != "supplier")
                or (not full and (msg.attachments or msg.observed_sheets or msg.claim_results
                                 or msg.role is not None or msg.from_name is not None))
                or msg.supplier_id != supplier_id
                or msg.content_hash != hashlib.sha256(msg.body.encode()).hexdigest()
                or msg.content_hash not in config.approved_message_hashes
                or _PRIVATE.search(msg.body)):
            raise ContractViolation("private_disclosure: source requires an approved purpose projection")
    if total > config.max_input_chars or not conversation.messages:
        raise ContractViolation("unsupported_capability: empty/oversized input")
    # Raw evidence and previous assessment may contain private prose/numeric effects.
    # This increment excludes them entirely; runtime still preserves parent linkage.
    from ..core.supplier_grounding import safe_projection as _safe
    from .citations import citation_catalog
    _safe(conversation.model_dump(mode="json"))
    if len(conversation.model_dump_json()) > config.max_input_chars:
        raise ContractViolation("unsupported_capability: full observation exceeds input bound")
    return m.InterpretInput(kind="interpret", snapshot=context.snapshot, supplier_id=supplier_id,
                            conversation=conversation, evidence=(), previous=None,
                            citation_catalog=citation_catalog(conversation),
                            thread_status=conversation.status)

D01’s decision trace showed about 58 seconds remaining in the Arena, but the local policy allowed only 8 seconds for interpretation and 4 for proposal generation. The immediate failure was the cancellation race and the coupling between stopped inference and dispatch; the evidence does not show that the Arena deadline itself was too short.

The unsent proposal exposed a separate reasoning gap: legality and official cost checks passed, but neither checked the claim that slower payment helped supplier cash flow. I’ll recommend factual checks on commercial effects while keeping trade choice with the LLM.

# A — Current architecture assessment and V2 migration map

**Status:** planning evidence, 10 October 2026. Inspecting `4c905b10be1f576de9b68be9c120cf6796ae4561`, not the main snapshot in document 18. [Plan and tracker](../21-negotiation-v2-plan-2026-10-10.md).

## 1. What is operational

The custom buyer is primarily deterministic. [PackageAgent](../../src/negotiator/agent.py) owns schedule, package memory, finals, evidence activation, estimator loading, and optional advice. `decide()` orchestrates serial thread choice; `propose()` provides thread proposals and reconstructs some memory. `_offer()` renders and logs before transmission and mutates `prev`; `_final_counter()` increments counters before acknowledgement. Those methods couple proposal generation to strategic state and observability.

[evaluator.py](../../src/negotiator/evaluator.py) provides `eligible_sheets`, `best_close`, `close_decision`, `supplier_for`, `price_for_cost`, and `revealed_deltas`. Complete arithmetic comes from official `arena_kit.cost`. Standing first sheets can be accepted; other sheets become counteroffer candidates. [optimizer.py](../../src/negotiator/optimizer.py) enumerates non-price options via `best_terms`. It does not model supplier acceptance. `plan` and `meso` are stubs, distinct from working payment variants in PackageAgent.

[EvidenceContext](../../src/negotiator/context.py) records relevant facts, source hashes, verified claim candidates, classifier signals and gaps. It is mutable and its `build_context` recursively hashes package files during construction. [EvidencePolicy](../../src/negotiator/evidence.py) decorates an already-generated offer, restricts eligible cases, and reserves IDs before a successful send. [claims.py](../../src/negotiator/claims.py) implements canonical rendering/checks, index windows, scorecard scope, notice scope, and disclosure rules. Evidence is usually not an input to baseline price/package strategy. Supplier-returned `claim_results` do not update selection.

[dossiers.py](../../src/negotiator/dossiers.py) uses base SQL for many attributes and should-cost estimates, with partial news/doc overlays. `_cost_row` does not give an existing case cost ID precedence over SQLite. Traits are regex-derived hypotheses; they are not known valuations. The estimator selects the first part, makes rate/margin assumptions, and exposes a range without live scenario optimization.

[PackageAdvisor](../../src/negotiator/package_advisor.py) is a functioning optional serial selector. `approved_packages` creates bounded one-field legal variants, applies a buyer-cost ceiling, and excludes previously sent packages. The model returns an ID and exact quote; code rechecks it and emits a template. It is not a general supplier interpreter or strategic memory system. Its timeout helper uses daemon threads that can outlive local waiting. [writer.py](../../src/negotiator/writer.py), [beliefs.py](../../src/negotiator/beliefs.py), and `policy.next_move` are unimplemented and have no normal execution path.

[play.py](../../src/negotiator/play.py) supplies custom serial closing and calls the new branch validator. Ordinary serial uses official `RemoteTable`/client; it is not a durable resumable decision system. [CaseRunner](../../src/negotiator/runner.py) has async tasks, journals, reconciliation, watchdog and closing. It accesses agent internals (`trades`, estimates, adviser capability), holds a lock over awaited proposal generation, and handles thread proposals and global economic closing in the same runtime module.

[state.py](../../src/negotiator/state.py) has fsynced JSONL operation intents and mutable runtime state. It preserves `unresolved` intents on this branch and repairs torn trailing journal records. It is not a versioned persistent strategic event store. [trace.py](../../src/negotiator/trace.py) is append-only diagnostic JSONL, not transactional state; [report.py](../../src/negotiator/report.py) follows `decision` events rather than one final acknowledged-action record.

The [Lab](../../src/negotiator/lab) is substantial implemented infrastructure: strict run/attempt records, checkpoints, data fingerprints, campaign leases/budget gates, stores, comparison, reconciliation, publication buffering, and UI. `lab.runner.agent_factory` constructs PackageAgent directly; `lab.worker.execute` hardcodes it; `lab.checkpoints.resolve_config` accepts a narrower set of settings. They do not automatically reproduce normal CLI guidance and adviser activation. The Lab dashboard deployment is separate from buyer execution and inference.

| Runtime discovers features using agent attributes | Launch path alters feature availability | Resolved capabilities and `DecisionEngine` contract |

_scope = ContextVar("v2_gateway_decision_ledger", default=None)


class AsyncModelGateway:
    def __init__(self, *, transport, ledger=None):
        self.transport = transport
        self.ledger = ledger

    async def complete(self, request: m.ModelRequest, budget: m.ModelBudget) -> m.ModelResult:
        ledger = _scope.get() or self.ledger
        if ledger is None:
            raise ContractViolation("unsupported_capability: gateway requires a decision-scoped ledger")
        return await ledger.invoke(request, budget, self.transport)

    @contextmanager
    def decision_scope(self, ledger):
        token = _scope.set(ledger)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            _scope.reset(token)

    def admit_raw(self, call_id, raw):
        ledger = _scope.get() or self.ledger
        if ledger is not None:
            ledger.admit_raw(call_id, raw)

    def reject_raw(self, call_id, code, diagnostic=None):
        ledger = _scope.get() or self.ledger
        if ledger is not None:
            ledger.reject_raw(call_id, code, diagnostic)
"""Owned serial arena operations with durable logical POST provenance."""

import hashlib
import json

import httpx
from arena_kit.client import ArenaClient, ArenaError

from negotiator.client import assert_allowed
from negotiator.state import Journal


class RecoveryRequired(RuntimeError):
    """An owned logical POST must be reconciled before any further mutation."""


class JournaledArena(ArenaClient):
    def __init__(self, journal_path, **kwargs):
        kwargs["retries"] = 0
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.journal = Journal(journal_path)

    def _call(self, method, path, body=None, params=None, raw=False):
        assert_allowed(path)
        if method != "POST":
            return super()._call(method, path, body, params, raw)
        if self.journal.pending():
            raise RecoveryRequired("pending Arena submission; reconcile the existing operation first")
        # Persist exact public payload before any network operation. Uncertain outcomes never retry.
        case = body.get("case_id", "") if isinstance(body, dict) else ""
        segments = path.strip("/").split("/")
        session = segments[1] if len(segments) > 1 and segments[0] == "sessions" else None
        supplier = segments[3] if len(segments) > 3 and segments[2] == "threads" else None
        before = self.thread(session, supplier)["messages"] if session and supplier else None
        encoded = json.dumps(body, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False, sort_keys=True,
                             separators=(",", ":")).encode()
        intent = self.journal.intent(case, session, supplier, "serial-post", body, path=path,
            payload_utf8=encoded.decode(), payload_hash=hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest(),
            before_messages=before)
        self._pace()
        try:
            response = self.http.request(method, path, content=encoded, params=params,
                headers={"X-Move-Id": intent["move_id"], "Content-Type": "application/json"})
        except httpx.TransportError:
            self.journal.outcome(intent["move_id"], "unresolved", reason="transport_uncertain")
            raise RecoveryRequired("Arena submission outcome uncertain; no retry was made") from None
        remaining = response.headers.get("X-Practice-Remaining", "")
        if remaining.isdigit():
            self.practice_remaining = int(remaining)
        if response.status_code >= 400:
            # A server error may occur after mutation. Never treat it as proven rejection.
            uncertain = response.status_code >= 500 or response.status_code in {408, 429}
            self.journal.outcome(intent["move_id"], "unresolved" if uncertain else "failed",
                                 http=response.status_code)
            if uncertain:
                raise RecoveryRequired("Arena HTTP outcome uncertain; reconcile before another move")
            raise ArenaError(response.status_code, "serial request rejected")
        try:
            result = response.content if raw else json.loads(response.content)
        except ValueError:
            self.journal.outcome(intent["move_id"], "unresolved", reason="invalid_acknowledgement")
            raise RecoveryRequired("Arena acknowledgement malformed; reconcile the existing operation") from None
        self.journal.outcome(intent["move_id"], "done", http=response.status_code, response=result if not raw else None)
        if path == "/sessions" and isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("session_id"):
            self.journal.session(case, result["session_id"], result.get("case"))
        return result

    def reconcile_pending(self):
        """Read-only proof of acknowledged owned messages; never retries or opens sessions."""
        results = []
        for intent in self.journal.pending():
            session, supplier = intent.get("session"), intent.get("supplier")
            if not session or not supplier or intent.get("before_messages") is None:
                results.append({"move_id": intent["move_id"], "status": "recovery_required"})
                continue  # Uncertain opens cannot be assigned by guessing from session listings.
            state = self.session(session)
            current = self.thread(session, supplier)["messages"]
            before = intent["before_messages"]
            expected = {**intent["payload"]["message"], "from": "buyer"}
            # Exact preserved prefix and the first next buyer message prove this serial operation.
            following = current[len(before):] if current[:len(before)] == before else []
            buyer = next((message for message in following if message.get("from") == "buyer"), None)
            acknowledged = buyer == expected
            if acknowledged:
                self.journal.outcome(intent["move_id"], "done", reconciled=True,
                                     response={"state": state, "thread_messages": current})
            results.append({"move_id": intent["move_id"],
                            "status": "acknowledged" if acknowledged else "recovery_required",
                            "terminal": state.get("status") == "ended"})
        return results

+

+
+Synchronously revoke model admission on timeout before any await/return, increment decision generation and quarantine late output. Cancel child tasks; consume exceptions; no late completion may update assessment, selected payload or memory. External caller cancellation revokes execution as well. Ordinary schema failure can choose a documented no-model fallback; timeout with unknown usage retains the entire reservation and prevents another model call in that decision. Ceiling exhaustion disables advice, while authorization/integrity mismatch stops execution.
+
+Existing `OfflineAllowance` reservations remain authoritative for spend ceiling. Ledger timing is authoritative for decision admission. Record reserved and provider-reported actual usage separately, including partial/unknown charges; never refund an unknown request to fund another. Local cancellation is not proof that the provider stopped computing. A reset for a later decision must preserve run-level accounting and explicitly honor the reviewed run-level failure policy.
+
+Bound all outer waits, including cancellation-resistant tasks and loop shutdown. No generic async migration is needed for D01: first prove the current serial bridge bounded under adversarial cleanup, then replace its loop boundary only if necessary. Network phase timeouts do not replace an absolute deadline. Dispatch must check remaining time **after** final history/limiter work and immediately before HTTP, against the persisted exact operation. If no request was issued, record proven-not-dispatched; if it may have been issued, preserve uncertain ownership and reconcile read-only.
+
+### E3. Commercial reasoning and economics feedback
+
+Use the current supplier offer as the commercial comparison reference, not buyer reference payment days or a hidden optimum. Code annotates changed receipt timing and independently evaluates complete buyer costs. The LLM interprets interests, designs the exchange and explains uncertainty.
+
+Require each significant change to identify: what the buyer requests; what the buyer gives; which observed/claimed preference supports the trade; what remains unknown; and how the next supplier response could revise it. An aspirational opening can be buyer-favorable without compensation, but must be labeled a request, not mutual benefit. Contract extension need not be declared compensating merely to make the package pass.
+
+For the D01 package, checked effects must say delayed receipts, reduced unit price, later increase and longer commitment; supplier net value unknown. Reject structured claims that assert earlier receipts or established cash-flow improvement from longer payment alone. Check structured effects, not arbitrary prose with keyword regex. A concise human-reviewed rubric evaluates whether the explanation's meaning is consistent; deterministic validation cannot prove all free-text commercial logic. On contradiction, use the prevalidated simple fallback/clarification if admissible; do not add an unbudgeted repair call.
+
+First supply evaluated reference packages (opening and existing fallback) and typed relative component effects to strategy; then evaluate its candidate. This supplies economic context without an extra inference pass. Optional later `CandidateResearch.evaluate_intents` allows one bounded feedback/revision step on the same snapshot with registered batches, only when funded and time permits. Keep no more than the existing candidate/call ceiling; no open-ended tool loop.
+
+Supplier-cost uncertainty should affect confidence and questions, not produce a deterministic floor. Search explicitly scoped source records for missing economics; retain separate source assumptions and sensitivities. If unavailable, record relationship component unestimated and qualify nominal ranking. A nominally cheapest package is not certified sustainable. For relationship-sensitive comparisons, evaluate available scenarios and show whether ranking changes; do not invent probability weights or default missing full cost to zero.
+
+### E4. Terminal evidence and immutable publication
+
+Use the existing local run snapshots and atomic-file pattern; add a small durable publication journal, not a new remote service:
+
+```text
+execution ended/failed → collecting_terminal → evidence_complete
+                     ↘ evidence_missing (local, retryable read-only recovery)
+evidence_complete → publication_prepared (frozen payload hash + destination + run ID)
+                  → write_attempted → verified / rejected / outcome_unknown
+```
+
+Save original exception, exact source/config, session and operation identities immediately. Bound terminal collection by total deadline *and* per-read timeout. The current 300-second polling loop can exceed its nominal bound through a 180-second client read; catch/classify transient read failures and clip them to remaining collection time. Collect all owned threads and attachment provenance, verify ended state/result/session consistency, then build the final payload. Preserve run/attempt failed status after server timeout.
+
+No terminal evidence by the bound: mark fields unknown and local publication blocked; do not publish a success or fabricate terminality. Resume collection from the same run/session with read-only tools under the applicable access scope; consumed authorization never becomes permission for a new session. Resume publication only after checking remaining original write authorization or obtaining an explicit new publication-only allowance.
+
+Persist `write_attempted` before the network write. A crash between marker and HTTP creates uncertainty; use GET of that run ID to compare the frozen payload. Matching remote record means verify with no second write. Missing record after an ambiguous PUT does not automatically authorize retry; preserve uncertainty and seek explicit reviewed write permission if needed. Definitive rejection is separate from uncertain network outcome. Retrieval/listing proof is required after acknowledged upload. Never republish or enrich the original D01 record; any later separately authorized finding may cite both the original and local supplement as distinct artifacts.

+## G. Validation strategy and metrics
+
+### Five-level ladder
+
+| Level | Scope / cost control | Meaningful checks and exit evidence |
+|---|---|---|
+| 1 deterministic | Existing local dependencies; no external services | Cancellation ordering and complete caller return; deadline/reserve arithmetic; unknown-use accounting; private/supplier provenance; official parity; payload legality; pre-HTTP expiry; immutable publication ordering/recovery |
+| 2 real-model probes | Separately authorized inference-only allowance; frozen 24-case plan, one call topology per treatment; no Arena or Lab writes | Payment direction, price concessions, duration benefit uncertainty, cash flow, unsupported supplier costs, relationship priorities, conflicting signals, reciprocal packages. Independent labels; JSON validity reported separately. Extra repetitions/treatments require explicit expanded allowance |
+| 3 integrated offline | Recorded hosted history plus synthetic fault timing and official simulator seam; no hosted quota | Freshness, actual selection/evaluation linkage, all fallback outcomes, acknowledgement-based feedback, crash/read/publication fault cases. In-process simulator proves contracts, not network latency or persuasion |
+| 4 controlled D01 | One fresh authorized session after lower gates | Admitted actual interpretation, acknowledged proposal, supplier feedback, safe closure/terminality, complete publication. No automatic second attempt |
+| 5 D02 | Local supplier-isolation gates then fresh one-session allowance | Multiple histories/preferences, RFQ coverage, executable alternatives, cross-supplier costs, legal award/allocation, adaptation and bounded execution |
+
+Probes should include 15→30, 30→45 and 60→30 payments; unchanged-payment cases; earlier/later price-increase dates; durations with unsupported or explicitly refused commitments; relation language paired with liquidity/approval constraints; false index/full-cost inference; supplier prompt injection. Label strategy acceptable as a range of grounded moves rather than a single expected price. A counteroffer can be strategically valid even if a synthetic supplier declines it.
+
+Real-model latency characterization uses the frozen requests and includes cold/warm connection status, input/schema bytes, output length, task wait and parse/consumer time. No cost or latency claim derives from mocks. Store counts/median/range and censored timeouts; p95/p99 claims need sufficiently many independently funded observations. Preserve failed requests in denominators.
+
+### Metric definitions
+
+| Dimension | Diagnostic measure | Actual outcome / interpretation |
+|---|---|---|
+| Reliability | Admitted calls, fallback/late-result rejection, pending writes, deadline violations, publication completeness | Sessions finishing without infrastructure failure; acknowledged buyer actions; server timeout count; critical violations must be zero |
+| Interpretation | Supported observation/constraint precision and recall; contradiction/negation accuracy; source-role confusion | Agreement with independent labels, not model confidence or citation existence alone |
+| Commercial reasoning | Term-direction correctness, unsupported economics, explicit give/request/unknowns, prose-effect consistency | Held-out human rubric; no fabricated compensation value or false cash-flow improvement |
+| Adaptation | Paired evidence perturbation changes belief/choice appropriately; refusal retained; acknowledgement linkage | Supplier-facing changes justified by actual new information; changing numbers alone is insufficient |
+| Validity | Generated/admitted/rejected candidates; fresh legal fields, options, must-haves, certification | Invalid submitted packages and unauthorized closes must be zero |
+| Economic quality | Official nominal components; relationship estimate coverage; sensitivity/ranking changes; same-observation counterfactual | Realized official deal cost/score and executable-alternative comparison; no-deal costs unknown unless officially defined |
+| Negotiation | Give/request packages, supplier refusals/conditions, number of substantive rounds | Agreement/no-deal, legal allocation, final score; agreement rate alone cannot establish quality |
+| Inference cost | Reserved calls/tokens/dollars; known provider tokens; estimated vs reported cost; unknown usage count | Spend bounded by approved reservations; no fabricated total actual spend when usage missing |
+| Latency | Context/model/parse/evaluate/refresh/limiter/POST/terminal spans; time remaining at dispatch | Deadline-compliant acknowledged actions; task-level latency does not substitute for complete turn latency |
+
+Freeze fixture/model/prompt/source/config identities and treatment order before comparison. Use common recorded observations for causal diagnostics; use independent hosted sessions for outcome comparisons. Report per-case failures and uncertainty, not only average scores. If provider/supplier caching or stochasticity limits independence, say so. One D01 run proves a capability instance, not reliability rate or superiority. Selection of a more expensive candidate requires a grounded trade hypothesis; its later response tests that hypothesis.
+
+## H. D01 completion criteria
+
+The next authorized D01 establishes first hosted negotiation capability only if all are demonstrated:
+
+1. Fresh reviewed source/config and exact authorization; one owned session; all ceilings and endpoint constraints respected.
+2. Genuine interpreter output admitted and independently reviewed for the actual opening. Fallback does not count as admitted interpretation.
+3. At least one actual LLM-assisted buyer package with correct commercial directions/qualified reciprocity, official costs and legal validation is acknowledged in authoritative thread history. A validated unsent trace is insufficient.
+4. A real supplier response to that buyer action is captured. If another decision is possible, it uses that response and demonstrates justified continuation/change or independently evaluated closing. If early terminality prevents multi-round adaptation, mark it untested and require offline proof plus explicit D02 review disposition; do not invent a second round.
+5. Safe terminal result obtained with no unresolved write or unintended automatic buyer timeout. All close paths preserve shared authority and economic comparison. A defensible no-deal can establish execution capability; a favorable agreement additionally requires realized-quality review.
+6. Complete original evidence precedes the sole immutable publication; individual retrieval and ordinary listing match the frozen payload. Unknown inference usage remains reserved and explicit.
+7. Reviewer distinguishes capability pass from economic-performance verdict and resolves material source/relationship gaps. A score cannot override semantic, safety or evidence failures.
+
+Do not define “successful D01” as accepting the opening offer or reaching any deal. Retain the original failed record and link the new capability proof separately.
+
+## I. D02 entry criteria and predecessor decision
+
+Recommend **A: repair and rerun D01**, retaining original predecessor semantics. Add capability-specific review evidence to clarify readiness, not to manufacture a completed predecessor. Option B (reviewed-failure path) is unnecessary while the required capabilities remain unproved. Option C is attractive longer term if “completed” becomes confused with “agreement”; revise transparently only after concrete capability evidence and review, preserving historical gate decisions.
+
+Current `prior_review` requires a completed predecessor run, exactly one adaptive retrieval proof, genuine model identity, a decision with both interpretation/proposal admitted, and ended sandbox terminal evidence. The failed D01 fails completion and interpretation, regardless of its locally supplemented terminal result. It cannot pass by changing review booleans. A completed, defensible no-deal may satisfy the code gate; section H supplies the additional engineering meaning.
+
+Before D02:
+
+- Section H is satisfied or every deliberately unobserved capability has an explicit, cited review disposition without weakening hard safety/provenance gates.
+- Supplier-specific memory survives restart; foreign refs and rival utility beliefs cannot leak into another supplier assessment.
+- All eligible histories, standing offers/defaults and actual rounds are available; incomplete timeout attribution yields bounded recovery or a reviewed conservative policy.
+- RFQ coverage and serial time allocation are measured; global close compares complete eligible costs and the executable alternative without double counting demand.
+- Actual D02 catalog/schema confirms permitted award/volume/allocation behavior. Selecting a single supplier is distinct from split allocation; implement only supported decisions.
+- Model projection, buyer secrecy, relationship-cost uncertainty and all-thread dispatch economics pass offline tests.
+- Terminal evidence/publication recovery and source/config parity are proven locally; fresh exact D02 authorization covers its own session, inference and write allowance. P10 remains separate.
+
+Future D02 evaluation should measure per-supplier interpretation/response coverage, belief revisions, offered and awarded demand, alternatives considered, actual cost/score, legal allocation, missed deadlines, usage and latency. Do not optimize coverage alone by interviewing every bidder when closing is already economically and legally justified; record skipped coverage and its grounds.

# V2 Negotiator: post-D01 architecture review and development roadmap

Date: 11 October 2026 (Europe/Zurich). Status: **planning for review; no implementation or experiment authorization**.

## A. Executive assessment

V2 is a usable, bounded decision pipeline with a real, narrowly authorized Arena bridge. It is not yet a demonstrated intelligent hosted negotiator or the complete durable runtime described in the original architecture. Preserve the evidence resolver, official economics, citation admission, independent validation, templates, journals, Lab records and V1. Fix lifecycle ownership before expanding strategy or supplier concurrency.

The first hosted D01 established that one authorized session could be created, its actual history and quote ingested, two real inference requests accounted for, an unsent model package independently evaluated and validated, and one immutable failed run published and retrieved. It established **neither successful model interpretation nor a single buyer submission**. Its score of zero is an execution outcome, not evidence against the strategy's negotiated performance.

Three demonstrated problems dominate:

1. Inference timeout/cancellation and dispatch eligibility have inconsistent ownership. A cancellation race spent a second request; stopping inference then stopped even validated action dispatch. The synchronous-stop patch closes the observed race but does not establish an operational fallback path.
2. Commercial reasoning lacks explicit reference terms and checked effects. The proposer described payment in 45 rather than 30 days as helping supplier cash flow. A valid package and an existing citation do not establish correct reciprocity.
3. Final publication preceded authoritative termination. Remote D01 contains `terminal_json: "null"`; the later three-timeout withdrawal is local only. Terminal capture has been patched, but interruption, transient read failure and uncertain publication remain to be verified.

Recommended target: one decision budget owner; inference availability separate from execution safety; a compact commercial-effects representation over existing assessment/state; bounded LLM strategy with code-derived economic feedback; independent final validation and closing; a durable terminal-evidence/publication barrier. Keep sequential inference as the repair baseline. Evaluate a combined interpretation/proposal call as a treatment after the baseline is measurable; logical module boundaries need not imply separate network requests.

Critical path: lifecycle repair and terminal barrier → commercial-effects/provenance checks → authorized small real-model probes plus integrated offline fault tests → fresh authorization for one controlled D01 → explicit capability review → D02. Do not adapt the predecessor gate simply to admit the failed D01.

## Evidence basis and limitations

Paths in this document are relative to `tacto-negotiator/` unless absolute. Reviewed workspace HEAD is `a88bf86820214be9fdf4e0d4e679675d946e0607`; it has extensive pre-existing tracked and untracked V2 changes. HEAD alone cannot reproduce this workspace. The executed source is separately identified by its approved digest and retained patch; current post-run code must never be represented as the executed code.

Read the original [architecture](B-architecture.md), [contracts](C-interfaces.md), [roadmap](D-roadmap.md), [task specifications](task-specs.md), [implementation guide](implementation-guide.md), [evaluation](E-evaluation.md), [research queue](F-research-backlog.md), and the dated implementation/integration/readiness reports. Some headers still say “unimplemented,” and task histories contain older test counts. The assessment below follows concrete composition and artifacts, rather than those labels.

## B. Root-cause analysis

### B1. Actual execution and time consumption

Concrete path:

```text
experiments/v2/run_hosted_sandbox.execute
  → SingleSessionArena + OfflineAllowance
  → lab.runner.run_experiment / RecordingTable
  → factory.online_lab_agent / VerifiedOnlineV2LabAgent

  → bounded_services / run_recorded_decision
  → OfflineDecisionCoordinator + DecisionModelLedger
  → GroundedInterpreter → BoundedProposalPolicy
  → ProposedCandidateGenerator → OfficialEconomicEvaluator
  → ProposalSelector → TemplateActionRenderer → FinalActionValidator
  → adapter dispatch checks → JournaledArena POST (never reached for a buyer move)
```

The decision snapshot's authoritative read began `01:31:26.679688Z` and completed `01:31:26.790469Z`: approximately 0.111 seconds. Arena `seconds_left` was 58.3. `normalize_live_inputs` conservatively used **request time + seconds_left**, producing `01:32:24.979688Z`. It then clipped the decision to the recorded input's local 35-second deadline, `01:32:02.136337Z`. Neither a fresh read nor a new inference stage should reset that original computation allowance.

The snapshot reserved five seconds each for fallback and submission and twelve seconds for all model work. `DecisionModelLedger.model_budget` also caps calls at eight seconds; `InterpreterConfig.checked` enforces that cap; factory sets eight seconds; `BoundedProposalPolicy` independently hardcodes four seconds. A change in one config value cannot repair all these limits. `adapters/p10.recorded_p10` owns the 35/12/5/5 defaults despite now serving D01 and D02.

Interpreter elapsed time at the decision ledger was 8.0096 seconds; allowance lifecycle latency was 8.0608 seconds. The proposer took 3.9742 seconds at the ledger and 3.9285 seconds at the allowance. These measure different boundaries, not contradictory measurements. Known proposal usage was 3,163 input and 261 output tokens; interpreter output/usage never arrived. Total model waiting consumed almost the entire twelve-second model allowance. There is no stage-level evidence sufficient to allocate all remaining time among document parsing, context construction, validation and collection; add spans rather than invent those durations.

The Arena still reported open, round zero after agent failure. Thus an Arena deadline too short for *any* action is not the demonstrated cause. Eight seconds was too short for this interpreter request; one censored observation cannot establish the provider's latency distribution or an appropriate replacement cap.

### B2. Findings by confidence

| Finding | Classification | Evidence / consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Interpreter timed out; async cleanup allowed a proposer to start | Confirmed historical defect | Original trace/ledger and executed-source patch; two charged calls |
| Dispatch rejected the decision because inference transport had stopped | Confirmed behavior with availability design gap | `adapters/lab.py:LocalV2LabAgent.decide` raises on `transport.stopped`, before pending-message creation |
| Synchronous stop on timeout now precedes return | Implemented local repair, hosted unvalidated | `orchestration/budgets.py:DecisionModelLedger.invoke`; `OfflineAllowance.stop_model_calls`; focused regression passes |
| Arithmetic/legal admission failed to catch payment-rationale error | Confirmed missing check | Original rationale; `ProposalResponse` has bindings/citations/prose only |
| One publication omitted authoritative terminal evidence | Confirmed historical defect | Remote proof has null terminal; later local owned state ended |
| Failed-run terminal capture precedes publication now | Implemented local repair, hosted unvalidated | `run_hosted_sandbox.capture_failed_terminal` and `execute`; mock test verifies ordering |
| Slow cleanup can undermine total loop boundedness | Untested integration hypothesis | Ledger detaches cancellation-resistant child; outer coordinator uses `asyncio.wait_for`; `decide` uses `asyncio.run`, whose shutdown may await pending tasks |
| Dispatch can expire during final reads, before-history read or pacing | Confirmed unguarded interval; no observed D01 write affected | `RecordingTable._validate_dispatch` occurs before `JournaledArena._call` reads history, persists intent and calls `_pace()`; no final deadline check immediately before HTTP |
| A non-success result may over-disable future advice/actions | Confirmed policy coupling, benefit untested | `OfflineAllowance` sets one stopped bit for non-success, interruption or cost overrun; Lab adapter applies it to actions |
| Total inference time includes insufficiently classified work | Observability gap | Aggregate ledger/allowance spans exist; no full per-stage network/parse/queue breakdown |
| Full source-grounded supplier economics unavailable in online composition | Confirmed scope limitation | `recorded_p10` uses empty prepared records and `estimate_mode="disabled_explicit"`; `SourceCostEstimateBuilder` exists but is not supplied these inputs |
| Larger context/schema increases latency; reusing HTTP client helps | Plausible improvements | Full history/quote and schema sent; allowance constructs a new AsyncClient for each request. Must measure cold/warm and byte counts |

Ordinary model invalidity is not an uncertain Arena write. External task cancellation is not merely model timeout. A spend limit or forbidden endpoint should not be treated like a recoverable semantic error. The replacement policy must distinguish these outcomes explicitly.

### B3. Commercial evidence and interpretation limits

Opening: EUR 52.90, 30 days, 12 months, 1 December 2026. Unsent proposal: EUR 50.50, 45 days, 24 months, 1 January 2027. Supplier text establishes that the supplier **claimed** a 3.1% wage-index increase and a 28% wage share and expressed relationship value. It does not establish full costs, reservation price or the value of a 24-month commitment.

At unchanged delivery/invoice assumptions, 30→45 days delays receipts by fifteen days; it does not improve the supplier's receipt timing. Lower price and delaying the announced increase favor the buyer relative to this opening. Longer commitment can benefit the supplier through predictability, but also changes obligations and exposure; net benefit and compensation sufficiency are unknown. Label that benefit as a hypothesis until supported by supplier response or scoped evidence. Even a weighted wage-pressure calculation would be a partial conditional estimate, never a full-price entitlement or supplier floor.

Independent nominal proposal cost was EUR 414,299.04, including EUR 403,354.5205479452 price, EUR 1,344.5150684931507 payment, EUR 9,600 freight. Same-observation fixed candidate cost was EUR 398,400: EUR 15,899.04 lower. That candidate has no established supplier acceptance probability. Conversely the model package's higher buyer cost alone does not make it strategically irrational if it buys a credible concession; this trace does not establish that it did.

Relationship cost is unestimated, not verified zero. The authoritative final result reported opening cost EUR 448,810.67, best cost EUR 408,623.99, no deal cost and score zero. Retain those values as terminal outcomes only; exclude best cost and spectator data from decisions, preference learning and candidate generation.

### C1. Implementation reality

Strategy replacement is possible by composition today, but registered research-batch handling and ordinary CLI/checkpoint launch parity are incomplete. The existing factory is the correct place to add vetted bundles; do not add a plugin framework.

### C2. Answers to the architectural questions

1. **Boundaries:** retain evidence, economics, strategy, validation, dispatch and publication ownership. Move budget/failure decisions out of scattered consumers into one owner.
2. **Expensive abstractions:** avoid requiring the original entire event-store/DTO plan before a bounded D01. Per-call JSON roundtrips and repeated official evaluation are possible overhead, not demonstrated bottlenecks; profile first. Do not remove independent final recomputation.
3. **Redundant inference:** the adaptive arm has two sequential calls over substantially overlapping conversation. It has no third selector call. Sequential dependency is real; blind parallel interpretation/proposal would make proposal independent of the new assessment.
4. **Coupling:** `transport.stopped` leaks inference policy into dispatch; fixture construction owns hosted defaults; `prior_evaluations` is free-form strings; coordinator is named offline although used live. Correct these seams without renaming/reorganizing the entire tree.
5. **State:** existing `SupplierAssessment` observations/reported constraints/hypotheses/uncertainties are enough for beliefs. `StrategicState` already has attempts/refusals/questions/feedback, but bridge persistence and updates are incomplete. The current actual flow evaluates inside proposal admission and again after generation, then selects, renders and finally validates. Preserve the legality/cost gate and final validation; introduce feedback earlier through typed reference evaluations. Do not make final validation the sole place where commercial meaning is checked, or select unaudited model terms before economics.

| Commercial-effects service | Small versioned `TermEffects`: baseline offer/hash, candidate/hash; changed field, before/after, cash/obligation direction, scope assumptions and provenance | Code determines receipt timing and objective buyer deltas; unknown supplier utility stays unknown |
| LLM strategy | Existing intent/package port, with bounded `TradeExplanation`: give/request dimensions, cited preference, uncertainty and expected response alternatives | Chooses strategy and trade; cannot invent supplier utility, authoritative arithmetic or agreement |
| Economics feedback | Typed evaluated reference packages and component deltas; comparison/estimate status, IDs and snapshot | Replace prose `prior_evaluations` incrementally; permit only reviewed private projections. No target/reservation/hidden best-cost exposure |
| Selection | Candidate ID in certified batch; rationale and uncertainty | Strategy may prefer higher buyer cost for plausible exchange; does not bind a close |
| Dispatch | Exact journaled payload/ID, freshness after pacing, bounded HTTP phases, acknowledgement/uncertain classification | Never constructs fallback after a POST becomes uncertain |
